description:
Sites: at least 17 locations across space.rs, message.rs, emoji.rs, contact.rs, position.rs, ban.rs flagged by clippy::manual_let_else under -W clippy::pedantic. Representative hits include space.rs:1195 (and 4+ siblings in the same file), ban.rs:237 / 278 / 487 / 586, plus apply_add_role / apply_remove_role at memory.rs:2181 / 2231.

Current pattern (one of many):

    let id_str = match id_val.as_str() {
        Some(s) => s,
        None => continue, // unreachable: validated above
    };

Idiomatic Rust since 1.65 (Nov 2022):

    let Some(id_str) = id_val.as_str() else { continue }; // unreachable: validated above

Five lines collapse to one; the noise-to-signal ratio improves; and the divergent control flow ('this path leaves the function or loop iteration') is signaled by the keyword instead of being buried in a match arm. This is exactly the pattern let...else was added for. The two memory.rs sites at 2181/2231 use unreachable!() instead of continue and benefit even more from the rewrite because the panic message lives next to the binding it documents.

What goes wrong if left: readability and signal-to-noise. The 5-line match is the dominant local-binding shape in handlers that do per-element validation, and every reviewer pays the cognitive cost of mentally collapsing it to its let-else equivalent. The MSRV for the workspace is well above 1.65 (the workspace freely uses async fn in trait, OnceLock, etc.), so the only reason these are still match-arm is convention drift from when they were first written.

One sweep bead, not 17 — the rewrite is mechanical and a single PR can sweep the file. Apply the rewrite under the same canonical-template propagation lens as JMAP-x2gd.52: check jmap-mail-server first since it's the canonical extension-server template, and propagate the sweep across all sibling extension-server crates. Standalone chat-server-only fix is fine if mail-server doesn't have the pattern.
title: manual_let_else: 17 'match { Some(s) => s, None => continue }' sites should use let...else (stable Rust 1.65+)
